controlled_change: Only expert_tail changes from wait to overlap; mixed 4/8-bit, packed Q8 rows 2, SIMD routing, 1848 CLOCK slots, eight readers and ready groups four remain fixed.
correctness: 59 native tests passed under Metal validation; all four normal conversations reproduce the prior confirmed output exactly, and all candidate decode phases exercise 1536 deferred tails with bounded drained ownership. Later full-model state qualification was skipped after the failed early screen.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Reduce decode wall time toward 200ms per token at unchanged arithmetic and 12GiB admission.
hypothesis: Encoding the next layer while the final expert groups run may recover tens of milliseconds from the observed submission gap.
limitations: Two short pairs have no confidence bounds and do not establish the 5 tokens/s target.
No normalization, outlier removal or favorable-sample selection was performed.
The trace gap includes instrumentation and next-layer preparation; it is not a predicted saving.
GPU-speed variation and process compression limit causal attribution; the option remains experimental with defaults unchanged.
outcome: Two complete alternating pairs failed the declared screen. Initial savings were +36.90ms and -67.30ms per token; append savings were -10.88ms and -3.28ms. Conversation ratios were 0.98497 and 1.06039. GPU timing varied and one candidate append reached 7.56GiB peak compression with 497771 decompressions, without positive net swap growth.
smallest_experiment: Keep expert_tail=wait. Measure temporary Metal allocation and retirement time before a bounded buffer-reuse candidate; both schedules still create 3238 buffers per decoded token.
